1. Dataset Identifier Range Reconciliation (`15` through `22` = 11 Distinct Datasets + 18-Table Spatial SQLite DB)

Why do identifiers 15 through 22 (8 root numbers) yield 11 new CSV/JSON datasets? Because identifier 21 (the Spatial Database package) is normalized into 4 distinct spatial entity datasets (21a, 21b, 21c, 21d) plus the 7 single-numbered datasets (15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 22) = 11 datasets (157 rows), all compiled into 21_task2_spatial_database.sqlite (18 tables) and 11_consolidated_database.sqlite (29 tables, 1,498 total rows).

2. Technical Architecture, Epistemic Methodology & Community Digital Twin Roadmap (Sections 11, 16 & 17)

Data Pipeline & Spatial Reference Architecture: Task 1 + Task 2 Validated Repository (85 projects, 205 documents, 452 sources) → Normalized Relational & Spatial Store (21_task2_spatial_database.sqlite / PostGIS-ready schema + dubai_sharjah_gis_bundle.geojson with 123 WGS84 EPSG:4326 features and exact nearest-vertex Haversine distance math) → Deterministic Spatial & Temporal Query Engine → Interactive 11-Layer Geospatial Map + Map-Linked Q&A Layer.

Strict Epistemic Guardrails (Zero Fabricated Telemetry & Two-Term BPR + Modelled Bottleneck-Delay Assumption Reproducibility): Every road capacity separates PUBLISHED_OFFICIAL (RTA/SRTA statutory corridor capacities and upgrade travel-time reduction targets) from HCM_7TH_EDITION_ESTIMATE. TomTom Dubai Traffic Index (SRC-436, https://www.tomtom.com/traffic-index/city/dubai/) is used strictly at the city-wide level (OBS-DXB-CITY-00: 31.3 km/h average speed, 19 min 10 sec per 10 km, 42.7% annual congestion, 26.3 km/h rush-hour average, 32.1 km/h AM rush [18 min 41 sec, 42.3% congestion], 22.6 km/h PM rush [26 min 33 sec, 94.4% congestion]). All 21 corridor-level speed, volume, and congestion records (OBS-DXB-001..015, OBS-SHJ-001..006) are classified as Modelled Corridor Estimates derived via a formula-based Uninterrupted BPR Link Term (t_BPR, v_BPR) + Modelled, HCM-Informed Bottleneck-Delay Assumption (+d_adj), and all daily HGV figures are classified as Scenario-Based Estimated Daily HGV Movements with 5 explicit modelling assumptions.
